The [VLM Run Gateway](https://docs.vlm.run/gateway/introduction) is an
OpenAI-compatible API in front of vision and speech models: OCR and
document parsing, visual question answering, segmentation, pose
estimation, multimodal embeddings and speech-to-text. Pixeltable’s
`vlmrun_gateway` module turns each of these into a computed column, so
images, PDFs and audio in your tables are processed as rows are
inserted.

### Prerequisites

- A VLM Run account with an API key
  ([app.vlm.run](https://app.vlm.run/dashboard/settings/api-keys))

### Important notes

- Gateway usage is billed per token, image, video or audio second, with
  a minimum of \$0.001 per call on most models (not embeddings or the
  partner Gemini, Kimi, MiniMax and Muse models)
  ([pricing](https://docs.vlm.run/gateway/pricing)).
  `chat_completions()` reports each call’s cost in `usage.cost`, as does
  `transcriptions()` in its JSON formats.
- Be mindful of sensitive data and consider security measures when
  integrating with external services.

First you’ll need to install the required libraries and enter your VLM
Run API key.



```python
import getpass
import os

if 'VLMRUN_API_KEY' not in os.environ:
    os.environ['VLMRUN_API_KEY'] = getpass.getpass(
        'Enter your VLM Run API key:'
    )
```

Now let’s create a Pixeltable directory to hold the tables for our demo.


```python
import json
import pixeltable as pxt
from pixeltable.functions import vlmrun_gateway

# Remove the 'vlmrun_gateway_demo' directory and its contents, if it exists
pxt.drop_dir('vlmrun_gateway_demo', force=True)
pxt.create_dir('vlmrun_gateway_demo')

SAMPLES = (
    'https://storage.googleapis.com/vlm-data-public-prod/hub/examples'
)
```

</pre>

## Read PDFs with OCR

`ocr()` sends a document to an OCR model and returns the Gateway’s JSON,
whose `pages` list has one record per page. The default model,
`paddlepaddle/paddleocr-vl-1.6`, reads each page as Markdown. Use
`pages` to read part of a long document. Pages are rasterized at 96 DPI
by default; dense tables, like the line items on this invoice, can come
back garbled at that resolution, so this example raises `dpi` to 150.


```python
docs = pxt.create_table('vlmrun_gateway_demo/docs', {'doc': pxt.Document})
docs.add_computed_column(pages=vlmrun_gateway.ocr(docs.doc, dpi=150))

# The first page's text, as Markdown
docs.add_computed_column(
    first_page=docs.pages.pages[0].content['items'][0].text
)
```

<pre style={{ 'margin': '-20px 20px 0px 20px', 'padding': '0px', 'background-color': 'transparent', 'color': 'black' }}>

To get text lines with bounding boxes instead, pick a model and method
that return regions, such as `model='paddleocr/pp-ocrv6', method='ocr'`.
Each model’s methods are listed in the [Gateway
docs](https://docs.vlm.run/gateway/methods).

## Extract structured data from images

`chat_completions()` works like the OpenAI endpoint of the same name.
Image columns can be referenced directly in messages. With
`response_format` set to a JSON schema, the model’s reply matches your
schema.


```python
receipts = pxt.create_table(
    'vlmrun_gateway_demo/receipts', {'image': pxt.Image}
)
messages = [
    {
        'role': 'user',
        'content': [
            {
                'type': 'text',
                'text': 'Extract the merchant and the total.',
            },
            {'type': 'image_url', 'image_url': receipts.image},
        ],
    }
]
receipt_schema = {
    'type': 'object',
    'properties': {
        'merchant': {'type': 'string'},
        'total': {'type': 'number'},
    },
    'required': ['merchant', 'total'],
}
receipts.add_computed_column(
    response=vlmrun_gateway.chat_completions(
        messages,
        model='qwen/qwen3.8-27b',
        model_kwargs={
            'response_format': {
                'type': 'json_schema',
                'json_schema': {
                    'name': 'receipt',
                    'schema': receipt_schema,
                },
            }
        },
    )
)


# The reply is a JSON string; parse it into a JSON column
@pxt.udf
def parse_json(s: str) -> pxt.Json:
    return json.loads(s)


receipts.add_computed_column(
    receipt=parse_json(receipts.response.choices[0].message.content)
)
```

<pre style={{ 'margin': '-20px 20px 0px 20px', 'padding': '0px', 'background-color': 'transparent', 'color': 'black' }}>

Added&nbsp;0&nbsp;column&nbsp;values&nbsp;with&nbsp;0&nbsp;errors&nbsp;in&nbsp;0.01&nbsp;s

## Segment objects

`analyze()` runs detection, segmentation and pose models. Here
`facebook/sam3.1` finds every object that matches a text prompt. Boxes
are normalized to the range 0 to 1, and `'mask_format': 'none'` in
`method_params` skips the masks. The bridge photo has no cars, so its
list is empty.


```python
photos = pxt.create_table(
    'vlmrun_gateway_demo/photos', {'image': pxt.Image}
)
photos.add_computed_column(
    cars=vlmrun_gateway.analyze(
        photos.image,
        model='facebook/sam3.1',
        method='segment',
        method_params={'prompt': 'car', 'mask_format': 'none'},
    )
)
photos.insert(
    [
        {'image': f'{SAMPLES}/image.caption/car.jpg'},
        {'image': f'{SAMPLES}/image.generation/sf-golden-gate.jpg'},
    ]
)
photos.select(photos.image, photos.cars.content['items']).collect()
```

## Search images with text

`embeddings()` puts text and images in one vector space, so an embedding
index on an image column can be searched with a text query.


```python
photos.add_embedding_index(
    photos.image,
    embedding=vlmrun_gateway.embeddings.using(
        model='qwen/qwen3-vl-embedding-2b'
    ),
)
sim = photos.image.similarity(string='a bridge over the water')
photos.order_by(sim, asc=False).limit(2).select(
    photos.image, sim
).collect()
```

<div style={{ 'margin': '0px 20px 0px 20px' }} dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: quartoRawHtml[3] }} />

## Transcribe audio

`transcriptions()` turns speech in an audio column into text, with
`nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3` by default. The sample here is a 10-second
clip, so the transcript ends mid-sentence. For timestamps, pass
`model_kwargs={'response_format': 'verbose_json', 'timestamp_granularities': ['segment', 'word']}`.


```python
audio = pxt.create_table(
    'vlmrun_gateway_demo/audio', {'audio': pxt.Audio}
)
audio.add_computed_column(
    transcript=vlmrun_gateway.transcriptions(audio.audio)
)
speech = f'{SAMPLES}/audio.transcription-summary/two_minute_rules.mp3'
audio.insert([{'audio': speech}])
audio.select(audio.transcript.text).collect()
```

## Rate limits

The Gateway allows 240 requests per minute and 10,000 per hour per
account, below Pixeltable’s default of 600 RPM. To stay under both, set
`rate_limit = 160` in the `vlmrun_gateway` section of your Pixeltable
config, or set the `VLMRUN_GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT` environment variable.
